title: Dispatch CSA 7: Returned Navigator Refuses to Leave the Institute
summary: One witness believes the first return must be allowed to happen.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Police cleared the square outside the Institute yesterday after a crowd demanded the destruction of the Calder aperture. Inside, the returned Mr. Rook refused an offer of evacuation. He says the three returnees cannot be certain they will survive a successful attempt to close the routes that brought them home.

“We are here because they set the anchor,” he told this newspaper. “If they do something else, tell me where we stand.” His companions do not agree with him. Professor Vey has supplied his younger self with every observation he recorded on the plain. Miss Bell continues to guide the receiver’s construction by signal.

Dr. Marr confirmed that the younger party has found a narrow passage marked by the receiver’s clear tone. It leads toward the original aperture, but the route changes whenever the anchor is moved. Miss Quill has proposed remaining at the stone long enough to release the spindle by hand while the others follow that tone.

It is the action described in the returned navigator’s hidden log. Miss Quill knows this. “He saw me let go,” she said in her last message. “He did not see where I went.” The Institute has asked her to wait while its staff considers another means of release. No alternative has yet been demonstrated.

At dusk, the returned Mr. Rook went to the window from which he had watched the departure. Witnesses say he remained there after the square emptied, facing the aperture as though waiting for someone to come through it.
